Pickens is also less involved in the play action passing game, which is not only a strength of Dallas’ but a rare weakness for Philly (even as of late). He drops off from a 21.6%→15.2% target share when Dallas runs play action, and his efficiency drops, sinking from a 14.1%→11.4% 1st down per route rate (-19.1%).

#Eagles went under center a season-high 30 of 66 (45.4%) snaps vs. the Raiders. They only marginally increased the rate they throw off play-action under center, from 17 to 20%.

Still, Jalen Hurts completed all four passes for 66 yards (backup Tanner McKee was 2 of 2 for 29 yards.)

The Eagles started the season not utilizing much of their under center game, or play-action passes from it. In the first six games, Hurts dropped to throw only five times. His numbers: 2 of 4 for 0 yards and a 7-yard scramble.

After the mini-bye, though, there was more under center with play-action passes. Hurts completed 5 of 7 passes for 147 yards and a TD vs. the Vikings and Giants.

But the Eagles didn't have as much success vs. the Packers and Lions (Hurts was 3 of 8 for 26 yards with a sack) and seemed to get away from it vs. the Cowboys and Bears the next two games as a result (Hurts was 2 of 3 for 6 yards).

The play-action pass game from under center has been efficient the last two games with Hurts completing 6 of 7 throws for 114 yards total.

The Sirianni-Hurts offenses have been predominantly been in shotgun, and have had overall success. The QB run game and Hurts' comfort have played a role in having more shotgun, among other reasons.

But he's seemingly improved throwing from under center. Continuing to marry the run with the pass and throwing more off play-action could be a conceivable way to improve the offense this late in the season.

What did Joe Brady do differently this past week comaprative to previous weeks? The Bills used pre-snap motion on 62% of plays, an increase from the original 50% average. Within these formations they allowed for a more innovative approach rather then consistently running zone reads & PA rollouts & TE screens in condensed 12 & 13 personnel formations. If a heavy usage of pre snap motion is utilized once again it forces DeMeco Ryan's to make adjustments to this coverage post snap. Houston has favorable matchups in the outside as it's looking like Keon Coleman is slowly being phased out of this offense, and Tyrell Shavers had an encouraging debut fitting into the X role. DeMeco Ryan's secondary is often aligned in cover 3 on early downs and transitions to two high safety & quarters/palms coverage on later downs, let's talk about Joe Brady's pass attack the adjustments they'll take to overcome this scheme. 

Joe Brady has to incorporate spread formations as Derek Stingley & Kamari Lassiter will be in press coverage at the line of scrimmage on later downs. The most sufficient route to creating seperation is on early downs, making James Cook & this rushing scheme operate in early downs where they can lean into more heavy personnel. Exploiting horizontal weaknesses in cover 3, by employing concepts such as stick or weak-side option routes which gives Buffalo's pass catchers leverage based choices that will be difficult for players like Henry To'oTo'o & EJ Speed as they haven't been the most formidable coverage linebackers. If DeMeco Ryan's picks up on the play sequencing which leans towards 1st down passing it's vital for Will Anderson Jr & Danielle Hunter to generate pressure vs Spencer Brown & Dion Dawkins. Houston has the 2nd highest pressure rate logged with these two at 41.5%.

Christian Benford has a shadow rate of 53.2% being 8th in the league, while Nico Collins has 2.16 yards per route run vs zone with a 34.1% red zone target%.

Looking at the final two Bengals’ series on offense, both stops by the Jets

One of the Joe Burrow narratives is that he tries to extend too many plays, and there has been the argument that Joe Flacco’s quick releases have helped the offense run with a different style over the last few weeks. The reality is though that you need to be able to draw upon that backyard style in high leverage moments. On several plays on the final two Bengals’ series, you can make the case that the best possible response would have been a QB scramble and giving an extended play a shot. Flacco has been unbelievable with the Bengals considering the circumstances. But that’s the limitation in his game, and it cost him, including on the sack where he got banged up on the sack. There were key plays where Flacco just got rid of the ball right away, as soon as possible, and tried to thread the needle to a covered receiver because trying to make a play outside of the pocket isn’t what he does.

The Jets doubled the heck out of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Andrei Iosivas has shown that he can make plays in those spots (see last year’s Chargers game), and I don’t put much of the result on the final two series on Iosivas. He got blown up on two of his three targets down the stretch, and that third target took a quick nosedive on him. Also, the first down throw on the final drive was way behind him. Again, Flacco has been terrific on the whole with the Bengals. But you wonder if the sack/getting banged up on the second-to-last series had a carry over effect that impacted the ball placement to some degree (also the second down run call if Flacco wasn’t zipping the ball at his best).

Ja’Marr Chase’s drop on the screen on the second-to-last drive also hurt.

Steelers-Bengals Burning Questions, #1:

What have the Steelers learned on defense from their debacle against the Bengals in Week 7?

Hopefully, lesson #1 centers on the urgency of covering JaMarr Chase. Chase had 16 catches for 161 yards in CIN's 33-31 win last month. It wasn't just the numbers, though, but the coverage busts that allowed Chase to run open most of the night.

The majority of PIT's problems in the secondary emanated from Chuck Clark and Juan Thornhill being unable to coordinate coverage successfully. Thornhill has since been released and Clark sent to the bench. PIT's new safety duo of Jalen Ramsey and Kyle Dugger have solidified communication since taking over two weeks ago. Teryl Austin's decision to simplify the scheme has helped, too. I expect much sounder execution from the secondary this time around.

The Steelers also struggled to pressure Joe Flacco in that first matchup. They had just two sacks and six QB hits, as Flacco carved up their zone looks with quick throws and good anticipation. Will the Steelers play more man coverage to bring pressure? Or can they drop seven and feel confident getting to Flacco with just four rushers?

Austin has begun to make use of a package that puts TJ Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig on the field together. Last week, those three combined for four of PIT's five sacks of Justin Herbert. That package was not in use in the first game vs. CIN, and could be a difference-maker this time around.

NFL Week 6 Observations

- Kansas City Chiefs: high end quarterback play and coaching is the best foundation for success in the NFL. Patrick Mahomes is positioned for his best season in years and he’s about to get back Rashee Rice.

- The Chiefs pass rush played it’s best football of the night, late. Overall, very strong effort against one of the league’s most talented offenses.

- After opening day I still had concerns about the Lions changes at coordinator, but this team beat the full throttle Ravens in Baltimore and gave a much more desperate Kansas City team a very contested game for 50 minutes. The Lions could have played better in some areas, but Jared Goff played another highly efficient game (until late when the pass rush became impactful) and Detroit is in a very good position to contend again in the NFC.

- That said next Monday against Tampa, I’d expect to see Detroit try to stretch the field a little more.

- I have a lot of notes from last Thursday Night’s Giants vs. Eagles clash, because that was an important game to evaluate on multiple fronts.

- Jaxson Dart played a very, very good game in a very big spot. You wouldn’t think it in the box score, but that outing from Dart impressed me more than any game Daniel Jones played as a Giant. Dart was accurate throughout the contest (something he was more uneven with in his first two starts) and he made a handful of very high difficulty, nuanced throws including two accurate throws where he took a hit on the chops. He had some heady runs, made good decisions, overall, genuinely impressive stuff.

- To use a hockey parallel, the second star of this game was the Giants OL as this was the best game they’ve played in years, but I want to give that two caveats. The first is Philly was down their top two disrupters in Nolan Smith and Jalen Carter (who would be the major issue for the Giants) and further, as my guy @DrakeFantasy said in the wake of that game, it’s important to understand that Philly’s defense is down significant talent from their Super Bowl team last year, and really over the last few years. So while this was still a very good performance from a rookie quarterback in a national spotlight, especially given Dart’s weak group of pass catchers, I don’t quite treat it as “the Giants beat the Eagles” because while they did, a Thursday night game, while Philly is down many starters from last year means the talent gap was much closer in this contest than it’s been in years on that side of the ball. So, still a very good performance, genuinely encouraging, but I wouldn’t treat it as Dart shredded an elite defense on Thursday.

- I’ll also say this game was a perfect example of why I value line play so much but don’t really care about the pressure stat, because it is like hits in baseball, as it lacks a ton of important context. Most of the pressures from the Philly side in this game were low value pressures. As an example, if a 3 technique (defensive tackle) beats a guard on their outside shoulder with a swim move and gains penetration early, that will be logged as a pressure and it will make the quarterback move, but unless that’s stacked with complimentary pressure from someone else, that pressure from the 3 technique is easily managed and less valuable than, say, an A gap blitzer beating the center, getting immediate penetration and then being able to pursue the quarterback. That A gap pressure is high value and changes the play, the other has a minor impact on its own, yet they are both logged as a pressure where, to use the hits parallel, one is a single and the other is a homer. Dart played well against the blitz and like I said above, he made two great throws while taking contact on the chops, but most of the pressure he faced was low value pressure and good chance his comfort level played a major role in his output.

- Back to giving Dart credit, one thing I noticed early in this contest is that Dart had better timing with Humphries than he’s had with most of his pass catchers, and a buddy of mine reminded me Dart played with Humphries more in preseason. That is encouraging for Dart’s future prospects, as his accuracy with the starters has a clear path to becoming more consistent.

- Ultimately, I’ve mentioned three names when it comes to Dart: Chrisitan Ponder (raw skill set), Derek Carr, Jordan Love as Dart’s range as I see it. He’s a better runner than Love or Carr (even though Dart and Carr’s combine were similar) and he’s more heady than Ponder, but this game showed that the higher end of that range is very much on the table.

- Now, I’d also say if Jalen Hurts plays well the Eagles still win this game. He missed a wide open DeVonta Smith on what would have been a 90+ yard score, and on the interception he threw late, AJ Brown was there for a score, in a one-on-one spot, on a crosser. Now I don’t put a ton of emphasis on “he should have made this read” analysis, because playing quarterback in the NFL is about executing under duress in very short periods of time, but just those two plays change that game. It’s the same when someone misses a throw, because all these guys miss throws when you watch all the games. That said, those were two very high leverage, very makeable throws.

- Hurts in general, I’ve said this for years, is the most unique quarterback evaluation of my lifetime. I hated him at Alabama. He looked like an entirely different guy at Oklahoma where many killed the Eagles for taking him in the second round, I totally got it. He’s had one MVP caliber season and two of his best games as a pro came in Super Bowls. He’s also had the best supporting cast in the league for years and he’s very inconsistent, where if he played at a high level more often, the Eagles would be nearly impossible to stop. So ultimately, Hurts has a lot of talent, where he can play with anyone when he’s on (just like Carr could and Love can) but Hurts isn’t as consistent as those upper echelon guys.

- To close with the Giants, I think the culture change stuff is being blown out of proportion. Brian Daboll gives Jaxson Dart bedroom eyes because given how well Jones is playing in Indianapolis, Daboll knows Dart playing well is Daboll’s only shot of being a head coach in the NFL after this season. Dart certainly seems charismatic, but did that charisma make Hurts miss those throws or compel Brian Burns to single handedly end a pair of drives? Is Dart’s personality making Cam Skattebo run like the fate of the world hangs on how much effort he expends? Lastly, and perhaps most hilarious, I hate to break it to everyone, but MetLife stadium was half filled with Eagles fans on Thursday night. The Dart/ Skattebo combination certainly makes the Giants more interesting, and I’m definitely a culture matters guy, but I’d still be careful overvaluing that component with this team right now. If anything, I could see Skattebo’s style being the most likely new variable to have an impact on current team culture (if they continue to be scrappy and win games, the culture thing could definitely be a factor, but that defense still played bad enough to give up 30+ points on Thursday despite the talent they have.)

- Last thought on that game, is Saquon Barkley interesting enough to have a documentary?

- Denver’s defense gave up less than 100 total yards while accumulating nine sacks, with eight different players in on that action. I’m a regression bettor, so I was expecting a sleepy game from the offense coming off their win in Philly, paired with this trip to Europe, but this defense has been excellent over the last three weeks.

- Once again, the Jets are in no man’s land as an organization now coming off one of the most inept offensive performances in recent memory. On the bright side, this was their defense’s best game of the season, and they have two very winnable games on deck against the Panthers and Bengals.

- Aaron Rodgers Steelers are now 4-1 with a Thursday night date with the Bengals on deck. Rodgers is no longer his perennial MVP contender self, but as I’ve said he was better than most gave him credit for last year and he’s been an obvious value add for the Steelers this season, who have the most decisive division lead in the league currently.

- Perhaps more importantly, Pittsburgh’s defense took care of business against a bad opponent, putting up six total sacks and 16 QB hits. CB Jalen Ramsey had two sacks, two tackles for a loss and two quarterback hits in one of the most outlier lines for a corner you’ll ever see. Ultimately the Steelers’ clearest path to success is to play their traditional stout defense, while Rodgers plays clean football while still having the capacity to win a few games late when necessary, like he did on opening day with the Jets.

- I do not overreact to early games from rookie quarterbacks, but I’ve never seen it in Dillon Gabriel. Cleveland is one of the few organizations in the league where the calls for Shedeur Sanders are not complete insanity and I would imagine he’ll see the field sometime this season.

- Cleveland should see what they can get for David Njoku, given the rise of Harold Fannin and the unfortunate reality that their season is over despite their high-end defense.

- Drake Maye came off a big boy game against a contender last Sunday night in Buffalo, and followed it up in the way high-end quarterbacks do: he carried his team to a victory over a talent-poor Saints team. Plain and simple, I’d call this the best two-game stretch of Maye’s young career.

- Despite the loss I continue to be impressed by Kellen Moore, as the Saints have now been a tough out in five of their first six games where I’d continue to frame them as an overachieving team, similar to how I felt about Dan Campbell’s Lions in his first season as Detroit honcho.

- Baltimore’s defense played up for the first time this season, and Derrick Henry roughly did what I expected, which collectively should have been enough to give the Rams a real scare (this game was tied at 3 at halftime) but Baltimore got absolutely nothing out of their passing game. Cooper Rush was benched for Tyler Huntley, where both players did next to nothing.

- The Rams were my preseason pick to win the NFC, and right now Detroit is the only NFC team that gives me any pause on that stance, but this was Matthew Stafford’s most uneven game of the year, and LA is lucky they didn’t lose this matchup.

- On the surface, Miami took the Chargers to the wire, where the Dolphins took back the lead late in the fourth quarter, but I’d frame it as Miami (with a good chunk of that on Tua) did a lot to give this game away. Miami heads to Cleveland next week, but their schedule from there: at Atl, vs. Bal (TNF), vs. Buf, Vs. Wash (Europe) is a stretch where things could genuinely unravel before their Week 12 bye.

- Regardless, I’m not sure what the Dolphins do long term, because this looks like a reset roster with a highly paid veteran quarterback that has not been very good this season.

- The Chargers have been ravaged by injuries, but strong quarterback play and coaching is what I’d pin this win on. This game was a prime example of why those two areas are the most important to winning. Also, LAC got 124 rushing yards out of Kimani Vidal despite their OL injuries. It was against a very weak opponent, granted, but still impressive given the state of their RB room and OL.

- Two vantage points on the Colts/ Cardinals. I said in my Saturday “Here’s What I’m Looking at” post that I could see Jacoby Brisset being good for this passing offense for just this one week, so him playing well didn’t surprise me. That said, I will spend all year waiting for the Colts to turn into a pumpkin, and what I can tell you is I had them in several survivor entries and this game was not even mildly fun to watch.

- I view Shane Steichen as a quality coach that would be an upgrade for a lot of teams, but I do not believe in Daniel Jones and I’ve been very critical of him his whole career. His first three games this season, shocked me. The last three have reminded me a lot of his play during his single playoff season with the Giants, where he was a game manager. That’s still a significant improvement against the baseline of his career, and I’d still call this the best six-game stretch of his career, but right now I’m viewing this through the lens that he’s solid (which again, is still a leap from where he was).

- Jacoby Brisset had 320 passing yards to the team’s cumulative 88 on the ground, and he orchestrated a 10 play, 78-yard drive where Arizona got inside the 10 to potentially take the lead near the end of the game, and that drive then stalled.

- I did not watch enough of Raiders/ Titans to have a real opinion, but the Titans offensive line allowed a number of dead on arrival pressures and apart from that, Cam Ward made several genuinely dreadful plays.

- Similarly, I did not see enough of Jags/ Seahawks to have a real opinion of that game, but Seattle’s pass rush impresses on a regular basis.

- I said on Saturday that I love a good revenge game narrative, but I don’t think Rico Dowdle is really in a revenge spot. Regardless, that man ran for 183 yards and added 56 through the air against his former team.

- The Panthers are in a difficult spot with Bryce Young long term, especially given the limitations of their roster. To this point Young does not look like a quarterback that’s going to lead a perennial playoff factor with some shot to contend for titles. He’s also shown enough where if you move on from him, pretty good chance you end up with a downgrade.

- Dak Prescott once again played very well, and as someone that liked the George Pickens trade, however that ends up from here that was a win. But this team can’t generate pressure and they gave up 199 rushing yards to the Panthers.

- Green Bay’s offense allowed Cincinnati to hang around into the second half, where the Bengals made this at least mildly uncomfortable for those in survivor pools.

- When I think of who Jordan Love is, he’s capable of spectacular performances where for one Sunday afternoon, he looks like an MVP contender, but he has enough middling games like this where he’s, for me, definitely behind guys like Dak Prescott still.

- Overall, the Packers won this game, but they showed very little against what is a weak Bengals roster led by a 40 year old quarterback that joined the team a few days ago.

- As expected, Joe Flacco made Cincinnati more live despite joining the team this week. Bengals tight ends saw 11 collective targets.

- Mac Jones had two turnovers, including the early pick that basically handed the Bucs their first score, but he also did a pretty good job of keeping this offense fairly competitive given how many starters were out.

- Fred Warner now has a season ending injury which means SF will be without their two best defenders through the rest of the year.

- Baker Mayfield has been very good all year, and today, given Tampa’s collective injuries, he did most of his work Sunday with reserve pass catchers.

Let's dive into the key aspects of this contest.

The Buccaneers offense gets a spark with the return of Chris Godwin Jr, this signify's many aspects of Josh Grizzards offense, including more empty set looks, which will have this bruised & battered O Line that's been steadily getting more healthy within the tackle spot of Tristan Wirfs & Luke Goedeke at full health, but Cody Mauch is now out and Ben Bredeson won't be playing this game 100%. More spread formations/drop back style of offense especially on early downs will be prominent in Josh Grizzard's attack, which the first matchup that comes to mind is Josh Sweat vs Tristan Wirfs. Josh Sweat has logged 39 pressures, 24 hurries & 9 sacks, while Tristan Wirfs has allowed 20 pressures, 4 hits & 2 sacks. In Tristan Wirfs return he's displayed his refined technique and the injury did not affect his agility whatsoever. Josh Sweat's bend and ability to flank within the D gap to generate interior pressure is certainly an aspect to look out for against this injured interior O Line.

Let's dive into the next vital aspect of this matchup which leads to the healthier receiving group of Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin & now Tez Johnson/Sterling Shepard rotating with Chris Godwin within the slot/outside looks. Jonathan Gannon's defensive scheme against Baker Mayfield will be prominent in neutralizing his deep ball playmaker, so I expect quarters coverage with two high safety shells at a high rate. Baker Mayfield has had limited time to throw in the pocket this season at 2.64 which ranks 21st in the league, however he has an escape rate of 5.3% being 5th in the league, and he has a pressured catchable rate of 57.3% being 5th in the league. Emeka Egbuka vs Will Johnson will be the most highlighted individual matchup in this game, Will Johnson will be bracketing/shadowing his side of the field. Will Johnson has a 35.9% shadow rate with a 1.5 target separation, which is a number that's gone down in his favor, however he's still lethal in press coverage, considerably in high leverage situations as well.

Let's talk about Todd Bowles defensive approach against Drew Petzing's scheme that's been a compliment to Jacoby Brissett's strongest traits as a QB. Todd Bowles is typically utilizing six man fronts and exotic blitz packages, he's used Tykee Smith in box safety looks + in simulated pressures & Jacob Parrish in these looks as well. Arizona's offense has a 9.64% rate of 13 personnel looks, and it's been heavily utilized at a higher rate due to the Cardinals backfield needing as much assistance in downhill blocking from TEs as they can receive. Yaya Diaby & Haason Reddick against all pro caliber Paris Johnson Jr & Kelvin Beachum who's replacing Jonah Williams is one of the key matchups in this contest, Yaya Diaby has logged 39 pressures, 26 hurries & 7 sacks. Haason Reddick being back in this matchup is crucial as Todd Bowles will lean towards four man rush sets early in the game. Marvin Harrison Jr is questionable to play however if he does he'll be against the prowess of Zyon McCollum, who's allowed a 1.4 target separation as well as a 65.1% catch rate. 

Baker Mayfield will overcome Jonathan Gannon's zone heavy scheme that operates out of a spot up/match up zone philosophy as Chris Godwin & Emeka Egbuka successfully stretch the field vertically & horizontally, and Todd Bowles implements stunts and heavy set pressure to overcome Drew Petzing's 12/13 personnel groupings.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs Atlanta Falcons 

Baker Mayfield looks to lead this tumultuous offensive group that's progressively getting more healthy against Kirk Cousins and a Falcons offensive scheme that's essentially failed to transition & tailor their veteran QB, let's breakdown the key elements to a vital divisional matchup for both teams.

Let's dive into the struggles of Josh Grizzard's play design and how it clashes with Raheem Morris' young secondary. Starting off with Baker Mayfield's efficiency in short yardage situations, earlier in the season, Baker Mayfield was attempting 16.4% of his passes beyond 20+ yards & completing 43.8% of them, that number has regressed to 12.5%, with Baker only connecting on 36.5%. It's been a vanilla style of play calling, and even with that, it hasn't been very efficient in short route concepts, let's talk about AJ Terrell against what looked like the offensive rookie of the year who's falling from grace in Emeka Egbuka, his yards per route run dropped off to 1.84, after being one of the highest in the leagues to start. Raheem Morris' scheme is a base 3-4 alignment with flexibility to switch to a 4-3 front, and the secondary typically is aligned in cover 3/two high shell looks contingent on opponents. AJ Terrell has a 1.2 target separation allowed on 7 pass breakups being 4th in the league, I'm intrigued to see how often Grizzard implements deep outs/crossers to stretch the defense horizontally. 

What has been the biggest transition for Zac Robinson's offense with Kirk Cousins being under center? Under Micheal Penix Jr this offense was at a heavy rate of pistol, which tailored to Micheal Penix Jr quick & decisive passing ability in shorter route concepts, where as Kirk Cousins in under center/play action has highlighted his ability to sell the play action & go through his progressions. Todd Bowles will probably be utilizing light boxes only on later downs, however on early downs I expect stacked boxes. Bijan Robinson has 4.45 yards created per touch, as well as 5.3 yards per carry against light boxes which he's seen at a 70.7% on his volume of rushes. Tampa Bay has the 18th ranked run stop win rate, believe it or not players like slot corner Jacob Parrish in the 2nd level can flank in the interior and makes stop consistently if minimalizing Lavonte David's presence against Atlanta's downhill rushing scheme is a goal of Zac Robinson, Jacob Parrish has 7 pressures, 2 sacks & 24 3rd down stops. 

Drake London being down in this game will make a player like Kyle Pitts more valued in the pass attack, and that includes in short concepts that Zac Robinson utilizes at a high rate, such as crossing routes, stick concepts & high-low reads in the intermediate area of the field. Jamel Dean has been one of the best coverage corners this season, he'll be utilized in a mix of zone & press man coverage, Jamel Dean the has lowest passer rating allowed when targeted at 56.3, a catch rate of 43.8% allowed, along with 1.0 target separation being 7th in the league. Some key tranch matchups impacting this game is Yaya Diaby against Jake Matthews, contingent to how often this offense operates in under center/play action, we'll see this matchup on an island consistently, similarly with rookies James Pearce Jr & Jalon Walker against Tristan Wirfs & Luke Goedeke. Yaya Diaby is up to 42 pressures, 27 hurries, 8 sacks & 7 hits, while Jake Matthews has allowed 28 pressures, 6 hits & 4 sacks. James Pearce is at a 14.7% pressure rate logged as well as Jalon Walker being productive with a 11% rate.

Kirk Cousins & this heavy set of under center/play action will run into a brick wall with Todd Bowles simulated pressures & exotic blitz packages, unless Bijan Robinson is utilized in spread formations/as a pure WR, this offense will struggle, while Josh Grizzard has a nice bounce back in terms of play design.

Fantasy Football Takeaways from Eagles vs Cowboys…

Dak Prescott
- Clear path to elite fantasy football ceiling this year. Multiple drops and penalties on long TD passes. Trade target.

Javonte Williams
- Walks like a workhorse. Talks like a workhorse. He’s a workhorse. Boring advanced metrics pushed ADP to R10- already paying off. 18 opportunities last night- clearest path to fantasy football greatness. Do not trade away.

CeeDee Lamb
- Best player in fantasy football ceiling. This is why he was a clear Tier 1 player and Top 4 overall pick. 13 targets is out of control. Feels as though his floor is 6+ catches for 100+ yards. Congrats if you drafted.

George Pickens
- Multiple missed or called back huge plays. One or two of them were in the end zone or right around it. Obviously not the game we were hoping for to start the season but could’ve boomed. Closer to 20 fantasy points than we all realize. Trade target. This DAL passing offense looked awesome- get a piece of it.

Jake Ferguson
- Similar to Pickens above. We’ll take 6 targets on 77% snaps from TE any day of the week in the final rounds of drafts. Was always a great late pick.

Jalen Hurts
- Simply a Top 4 QB every single week.

Saquon Barkley
- Very casual 23 opportunities for 18.4 fantasy points. Feel like we take the greatness for granted- I am guilty of that for sure. Top 5 RB floor if he plays anywhere near 17 games.

Will Shipley/AJ Dillon
- Monitor the Shipley injury. Whoever is RB2 must be rostered as they had standalone value last night as more than just a Saquon handcuff.

AJ Brown
- Worst pick in Round 2 of drafts for the second year in a row. It had to be said- don’t care that we are only one game in. Top 12 WR in just three of last eleven games played. Completely up to chance every week if he is the number one scoring option, or number four, in this PHI offense. No denying he is a monster real-life WR. An absolute beast. But for fantasy football purposes, AJB has a floor of 1 point and a ceiling of 40 points. There are at least 20 other WRs who share those outcomes. I am almost certain he’ll be force-fed targets next week. I am almost certain he’ll finish Top 18 at the position in points per game. But taking him over Ladd, Jacobs, Bucky, Higgins, etc. was never the move. All offseason I was criticized for my ranking of AJB around WR20… Trade away for WR1 value if possible- there are plenty of managers interested.

DeVonta Smith
- Why roster AJB when you can just roster Smith for half the trade cost? Honestly.

Dallas Goedert
- Viable TE streamer option when the Eagles will have to put up points.

Thursday Night Football

Detroit Lions vs Dallas Cowboys

Starting off the final month of the regular season, were gifted with an extraordinary matchup between Dak Prescott after a statement win vs Dan Campbell's offense prior to just falling short in a crucial divisional game. Let's dive into the key matchups of this one.

The addition of Quinnen Williams continues to pay dividends for Matt Eberflus' defense, Dallas' rush defense went from one of the worst units in terms of output with yards given up at 143 yards a game (29th) to it now being down to 45 yards a game (1st). Quinnen Williams leads all DTs with a 47.2% run stop win rate. This is the area of this matchup I'd like to dive into first considering Detroit may be down Sam Laporta, & valuable blocking TE Brock Wright for a 2nd straight week, they'll struggle to adapt under center/play action which is a prominent entity to Dan Campbell's success. The key outside matchup being Amon Ra St Brown as a pure vertical threat stretching the field out against Shavon Revel who's displayed very refined instincts and may even be taking over the CB1 role. Amon Ra has 2.72 yards per route run as well as 1.67 target separation vs zone, while Shavon Revel has allowed a 72.7% catch rate on 1.4 target separation. 

Lets analyze the pass attack on Brian Schottenheimer's end against a Kelvin Sheppard defense that's been in zone coverage at a 58.5% rate and in man coverage at a 35.5% rate. DJ Reed coming back has been nothing short of glaring, he's allowed Kelvin Sheppard's defense to be in man coverage in high leverage 3rd down sitautions. With Terrion Arnold out for the season, we'll see the duo of DJ Reed & Rock Ya Sin against George Pickens & Ceedee Lamb who've become one of the better duos in football. George Pickens has played more of a WR1 role in this scheme, therefore he'll be against DJ Reed, who in a minimal volume of snaps has allowed only 1.0 target separation with a 58.3% catch rate allowed, eorge Pickens has been massively dominant with 0.141 first downs per route run (4th), 2.68 yards per route run (5th), & 15.6 yards per reception. Ceedee Lamb likely will be utilized as both a horizontal & vertical threat, highlighting his speed in underneath routes against Amik Robertson, and more of his separation/point of catch ability against Rock Ya Sin. 

The trench play in this matchup is vital, and that’s where I’ll dive into Matt Eberflus & Kelvin Sheppard’s defensive schemes. Matt Eberflus has had a lower-than-average blitz rate, which stands at 21.7%, which pertains to how often they’re capable of generating pressure with a 4 man rush. Donovan Ezeriuaku has stolen Abdul Carter’s title as the most productive and well rounded rookie edge rusher. He’s logged 28 pressure, 15 hurries & 11 hits, and is viable component In exotic blitz’s and stunts. Majority of this O Line is banged up, including superstar Penei Sewell. He’s arguably one of the leagues most well rounded tackles, and he’ll eliminate how often Eberflus generates pressure against Detroit’s shotgun looks. This offense has thrived in run-first/under center plays action formations, as they have a shotgun rate of 35.3% this season. Flipping over to Dak Prescott, he's been one of the leagues most top notch improvisers with a pressured catchable pass rate of 62.3% (1st), & a 78.6% blitzed catchable rate (2nd). We'll see Aidan Hutchinson who has 71 pressures, 46 hurries & 15 sacks against a Cowboys pass protection that has made a considerable jump accredited to the addition of Tyler Booker, who has them at 13th in pass block win rate. 

This game really feels like it's all the marbles for whoever wins, and a Lions team that just lost their CB2 in Terrion Arnold, and being plagued with injuries on offense with both TEs who are utilized in many different facets to assist the rushing attack + Jared Goff is going to struggle expeditiously, against an up & coming defensive line week after week.

- Veteran PIT QB Aaron Rodgers dialed back the hand of time against his former team, throwing for four touchdowns on the day. Completing 73% of his own passes (22/30) for 244 passing yards.

-  4th-Year NYJ WR Garrett Wilson and his former college teammate Justin Fields picked up right where they left off from their Ohio State days. Wilson caught seven of his nine targets for 95 receiving yards and a TD grab.

• The young gun in Drake Maye hosting the veteran Aaron Rodgers and this Arthur Smith offense, a lot of noteable and polarizing matchups to dive into. Mostly pertaining Drake Maye's ability to evade pressure and process this highly touted secondary.

• New Englands offensive line has been fairly above average. The interior OL with Jared Wilson, Garrett Bradbury and Mike Onwenu will struggle significantly if Josh McDaniels incorporates more pistol looks then pre-snap motion TE/RB screens.

• Arthur Smith culminated in his career heavy play action and outside zone looks for his offense, including bootleg, TE screens etc. Aaron Rodgers with his regressed mobility and more pocket operating based game fits this scheme perfectly. With that said it presages the idea that  Mike Vrabel being innovative with his approach is vital. The one gap scheme has been successful, but you have to neutralize the 12 personnel. Leverage and creating YAC is the formula and Jaylen Warren is the catalyst.

Steelers IOL led by Zach Frazier, has started off the year with some ups and downs. Let's see if Arthur Smiths scheme can leverage them to more favorable looks in the trenches.
